source_text: Hodie perennis virtutis texuntur coronae. Hodie sacra benevolorum, et religiosorum, diesque festos studiose colentium capita coronare volens Deus, firmae fidei amatores tanquam vocatos et heredes appellat; supernumque regnum cum studio eos qui caelestia sapiunt, ut se divino incorporeorum chororum ministerio coniungant, vocat. Hodie Davidicum adimpletum est oraculum, quod dicit: Laetentur caeli, et exultet terra. Gaudebunt campi, et omnia ligna sylvae, a conspectu Domini quoniam venit. Et David quidem, ligna dicit: Praecursor vero Domini, arbores facientes fructus dignos paenitentia, immo Domini adventu, nuncupat. At Dominus noster Iesus Christus, perenne gaudium cunctis in ipsum credentibus adnunciat. Ait enim: Videbo vos, et gaudebitis: et gaudium vestrum nemo tollet a vobis. Hodie celebre atque ineffabile Christianorum, qui suam in Christum spem sponte obsignarunt, mysterium plane nobis adnunciatur. Hodie Gabriel, qui Deo assistit, ad castissimam Virginem veniens, illud, Ave gratia plena, ipsi adnunciat. Ipsa vero secum cogitante qualis esset illa salutatio: Angelus confestim subiunxit, dicens: Dominus tecum. ne timeas Maria: invenisti enim gratiam apud Deum. Ideo concipies in utero, et paries filium: et vocabunt nomen eius Iesum. Hic erit magnus, et filius Altissimi vocabitur. Et dabit ipsi Dominus Deus sedem David patris eius, et regnabit in Domo Iacob in aeternum: et regni eius non erit finis. Dixit autem Maria ad Angelum: Quomodo istud fiet mihi: quoniam virum non cognosco? nunquid amplius virgo permanebo? nunquid virginitatis dignitas in me prodetur et amittetur? Quae, dum velut admirabunda, secum animo sanctissima Virgo versaret; breviter Angelus sermonis summam profert, ac dicit: Spiritus sanctus superveniet in te, et virtus Altissimi obumbrabit tibi. Ideoque et quod nascetur ex te sanctum, vocabitur filius Dei. Nam quod est, hoc et omnino vocabitur. Convenienter igitur sanctam Mariam ex omnibus generationibus solam gratia elegit.
thought_title: The feast crowns the faithful and fulfills David's oracle; Gabriel announces to Mary
orientation: The homilist proclaims that today God crowns the faithful and calls them heirs, fulfills David's prophecy of cosmic joy, cites Jesus' promise of lasting joy, and narrates Gabriel's announcement to Mary and her question, ending with the angel's explanation that the Holy Spirit will overshadow her and the child will be called Son of God.

pass_b_english: Today crowns of enduring virtue are woven. Today God crowns the heads of the benevolent and the devout, of those who zealously keep the feast days, calling lovers of firm faith as ones called and heirs. And the heavenly kingdom zealously summons those who have wisdom for heavenly things to join the divine ministry of the angelic choirs. Today David's oracle is fulfilled, which says: "Let the heavens rejoice, and let the earth exult. The fields will be glad, and all the trees of the forest before the face of the Lord, because he comes." David indeed speaks of trees; the Forerunner of the Lord, however, calls them trees producing fruits worthy of repentance, or rather, worthy of the Lord's coming. But our Lord Jesus Christ announces lasting joy to all who believe in him. For he says: "I will see you, and you will rejoice; and no one will take your joy from you." Today the celebrated and ineffable mystery of Christians, who have voluntarily sealed their hope in Christ, is plainly announced to us. Today Gabriel, who stands before God, coming to the most chaste Virgin, announces to her: "Hail, full of grace." She, however, pondering within herself what kind of greeting this might be, the angel immediately adds, saying: "The Lord is with you. Do not fear, Mary; for you have found favor with God. Therefore you will conceive in your womb and bear a son, and they will call his name Jesus. He will be great, and will be called Son of the Most High. And the Lord God will give him the throne of his father David, and he will reign in the house of Jacob forever; and there will be no end to his kingdom." Mary said to the angel: "How will this happen to me, since I do not know a man? Will I remain a virgin still? Will the dignity of virginity in me be betrayed and lost?" While the most holy Virgin turned these things over in her mind as if marveling, the angel briefly sets forth the sum of his speech and says: "The Holy Spirit will come upon you, and the power of the Most High will overshadow you. Therefore also the holy one to be born from you will be called Son of God. For what he is, that indeed he will also be called." Accordingly, therefore, holy Mary alone among all generations is chosen by grace.

problems.quote: He summons those who have wisdom for heavenly things to join the ministry of the angelic choirs.
problems.source_quote: supernumque regnum cum studio eos qui caelestia sapiunt, ut se divino incorporeorum chororum ministerio coniungant, vocat.
problems.why: Drops 'the heavenly kingdom' (supernumque regnum) as the subject and replaces it with 'He' (God), also omitting 'zealously' (cum studio) and 'divine' (divino).
problems.fix: And the heavenly kingdom zealously summons those who set their minds on heavenly things to join the divine ministry of the angelic choirs.

problems.quote: Will the dignity of virginity in me be proved and lost?
problems.source_quote: nunquid virginitatis dignitas in me prodetur et amittetur?
problems.why: Confuses prodetur (from prodo, 'be betrayed/forfeited') with probabitur ('be proved').
problems.fix: Will the dignity of virginity in me be betrayed and lost?

problems.quote: or rather, calls them by the Lord's advent.
problems.why: Domini adventu is parallel to paenitentia with dignos ('worthy of repentance, or rather of the Lord's coming'), not an instrumental phrase with nuncupat.
problems.fix: or rather, worthy of the Lord's coming.
problems.ruling: immo Domini adventu parallels dignos paenitentia (fruits worthy), not nuncupat; English wrongly ties advent to naming.

problems.quote: For what is, that also will be called altogether.
problems.source_quote: Nam quod est, hoc et omnino vocabitur.
problems.why: Misreads the subject ('what he is') as 'what is' and renders omnino ('certainly/indeed') as 'altogether,' yielding a garbled sentence.
problems.fix: For what he is, that indeed he will also be called.
problems.ruling: quod est is 'what he is'; omnino means certainly, not altogether; English is garbled and loses the sense.

edits.old: He summons those who have wisdom for heavenly things to join the ministry of the angelic choirs.
edits.new: And the heavenly kingdom zealously summons those who have wisdom for heavenly things to join the divine ministry of the angelic choirs.

edits.old: Will the dignity of virginity in me be proved and lost?
edits.new: Will the dignity of virginity in me be betrayed and lost?

edits.old: or rather, calls them by the Lord's advent.
edits.new: or rather, worthy of the Lord's coming.

edits.old: For what is, that also will be called altogether.
edits.new: For what he is, that indeed he will also be called.

fixed: agency: restored subject 'heavenly kingdom' from 'supernumque regnum ... vocat' and added 'zealously' for 'cum studio' and 'divine' for 'divino'.
mistranslation prodetur: changed 'proved' to 'betrayed' since source 'prodetur' is from prodo, not probabitur.
mistranslation adventu: changed instrumental 'by the Lord's advent' to 'worthy of the Lord's coming' since 'Domini adventu' parallels 'paenitentia' under 'dignos'.
mistranslation quod est: changed to 'what he is ... indeed' since 'quod est' refers to the child and 'omnino' means indeed, not altogether.

problems.quote: calling them lovers of firm faith, as ones called and heirs.
problems.source_quote: firmae fidei amatores tanquam vocatos et heredes appellat;
problems.why: Misreads syntax: firmae fidei amatores is the direct object of appellat, not a predicate applied to 'them'; God calls lovers of firm faith 'called' and 'heirs.'
problems.fix: calls lovers of firm faith as ones called and heirs.
problems.ruling: appellat governs firmae fidei amatores; tanquam vocatos et heredes names them, not a separate 'them' titled amatores.

edits.old: calling them lovers of firm faith, as ones called and heirs.
edits.new: calling lovers of firm faith as ones called and heirs.

fixed: mistranslation lovers: edited — source 'firmae fidei amatores tanquam vocatos et heredes appellat' makes amatores the object called 'vocatos et heredes'.
heavenly kingdom summons: no edit — source 'supernumque regnum ... vocat' supports kingdom as subject.
betrayed and lost: no edit — source 'prodetur et amittetur' supports betrayed, not proved.
worthy of the Lord's coming: no edit — source 'immo Domini adventu' elides dignos, ablative of worthy.
For what he is: no edit — source 'Nam quod est, hoc et omnino vocabitur' refers to the child; 'he' fits without misstating.
